In Summary
- The CMF Buds Neo are the latest TWS from Nothing’s sub-brand, CMF.
- The new buds come in attractive colors, in true CMF tradition, and punch above their price point in terms of specs and features.
- At Rs 1999, the CMF Buds Neo are the most affordable TWS in CMF’s audio portfolio, and have also been called the most accessible entry point to the CMF ecosystem. They do face a lot of competition, though.
While it is hard being a new smartphone in this tech climate, we believe it is harder being a new pair of TWS. The number of new TWS, as well as increasingly competitive prices and features across a wide range of price brackets, make it quite a task for a new pair to make its mark in the tech world. The latest addition in this lineup comes from Nothing’s sub-brand CMF, the CMF Buds Neo. Priced at Rs. 1,999, the Buds Neo are positioned as the most accessible entry to the CMF ecosystem. They come with an impressive feature list and a quirky design. But is that enough to help the CMF Buds Neo make space for itself in the TWS market?
CMF Buds Neo Appearance and Design: Typically CMF, Geometry with some flair
CMF, like its parent company Nothing, speaks a very distinct design language. A language no one else in the industry has adopted (yet) – a very smooth blend of Nothing’s industrial design combined with CMF’s bright colored flair. The CMF Buds Neo speak this language. Their square-shaped case comes with soft, rounded edges that make it sit very comfortably in one’s hands. The top left corner has a tactile, round dial. This is not just a design touch but also has some utility – it can be used to attach a lanyard that will keep your Buds Neo from getting lost.
The buds come in three different colors: Black, White, and Dark Blue. The Dark Blue and White color options bring very vibrant color contrasts with green and orange ear tips and tactile dials, respectively, while the Black is all black. The white variant, whose white case comes with a super bright orange tactile dial, is perhaps the most distinct. There is a small ‘CMF by Nothing’ badge in orange on the front as well. The cases have a matte finish while the dials are glossy.
The case has a very tiny LED light on the front and a USB Type-C port on the back. Flip the case open, and you find the buds resting nicely inside, with a ‘Buds Neo’ branding slightly above the earbuds. The buds come with a typical TWS design – a bulbous head attached to a long pill-shaped stem. The eartips bring the pop of orange to the white buds, while the texture of the overall buds is a mix of glossy and matte.
There is a small glossy dot on the head of the stem of the right bud and a thick, slightly raised circle on the stem of the left bud. The buds are comfortable to wear and come with one set of eartips attached and two others in the box. We used the medium-sized eartips, and they fit snugly. Speaking of snug fits, the buds also attach magnetically to the case.
The CMF Buds Neo case itself is quite compact – it is square, with length and breadth both at 54.3 mm, and is a little thick at 23 mm. It weighs 50.3 grams, while the buds weigh just a little over 4 grams each. The case is very pocket-friendly, and the buds are light on the ear. The buds come with an IP55 rating, making them good enough for sweaty gym sessions, while the case has an IPX rating, making it splash-proof, which is handy (most TWS cases still do not have splash resistance).
The white case does get dirty very easily (it caught dirt marks in our bag), but all in all, the design of the CMF Buds Neo is very eye-catching and definitely something not-so-usual. If you are not into pops of color, you can choose the black variant. Those who want to be right between these two extremes can go for the blue variant, with its flash of green eartips and disk.
CMF Buds Neo Specs and Controls: Very impressive at this price point
The CMF Buds Neo come with impressive specs for their price. They have 12.4 mm dynamic drivers with a 20 Hz- 20 kHz frequency response, two mics per earbud (for a total of four), Bluetooth 6.0, support for AAC and SBC codecs, and ANC of up to 35 dB. There is also support for spatial audio, and you get six EQ presets. All of these features are accessible through the NothingX App. The case comes with a 460 mAh battery with support for fast charging, and each earbud has a 45 mAh battery in it as well. The buds support Google Fast Pair, Microsoft Swift Pair, and also Dual-Device connectivity.
Pairing the CMF Buds Neo is simple: you flip the case open, wait for the buds to appear in your device’s Bluetooth list, and select them. To get the buds in pairing mode to connect with other devices, you can simply tap and hold the stem of the buds for five seconds, then select them from your device’s Bluetooth list. The controls on the buds are basically a series of taps- double-tapping on either bud will take you to the next track or reject a call; triple-tapping will take you to the previous song, while tapping and holding will let you switch between ANC and transparency mode.
No action is assigned to the double-tap-and-hold, but one can assign it to increasing or decreasing the volume or summoning the voice assistant. Apart from the call functionality, these controls can be customized using the Nothing X app. Interestingly, there is no option to map a control to a single tap, perhaps out of concern for accidental touches.
CMF Buds Neo Performance: Good audio, decent ANC and very good calling
The 12.4 mm dynamic drivers on the CMF Buds Neo come with a titanium-coated PET dome and a flexible PEEK and PU surround. This, as per Nothing, adds a bass-ful punch to the audio while ensuring vocals do not get muddied. The buds certainly deliver on both these fronts. The audio is full-bodied, and while it does focus a bit on bass, it does not drown out the treble or vocals. It is not balanced in a way that would give an audiophile an eargasm, but we seldom see that at this price anyway. On the other hand, they will impress casual listeners in a heartbeat, delivering a thoroughly enjoyable experience in pop, Bollywood, R&B, and hip-hop, and similar genres.
The Nothing X app comes with six EQ presets, and each one offers a distinct sound profile, which sometimes is not the case in this price segment. There is also the option to create an EQ based on one’s own preferences. The buds provide a reasonably spacious sound, which is usually not very easy for TWS to achieve, especially at this price point. The sound obviously does not feel as immersive as some of the high-end audio gear available on the market, but for the price, it is a hit in our books. The vocals are sharp enough to listen to hour-long podcasts or watch content.
The CMF Buds Neo also come with ANC. There are four options – low, medium, high, and adaptive. We mostly stuck to the ‘high’ setting. It will not cancel out very loud noises, but the snug fit of the buds combined with effective ANC does kill environmental noise with ease. It managed to drown out noise in a crowded cafe very effectively. We could not hear our friend sitting across from us with ANC on. The transparency mode brings back awareness to what would otherwise be a very isolating experience – the conversation we were not able to hear earlier became clear with transparency mode.
The call quality of the buds is very good as well – a pleasant surprise at this price point. We did not have any issues hearing the caller and did not get any complaints about our voice quality either. There is a low latency mode for games, but we had to turn it on manually, which was a bit of a pain.
The controls of the CMF Buds Neo are easy to remember but take some serious getting used to. We often found we had to tap harder than we are used to in order to register a command. The buds also lack wear detection, which means the audio does not automatically pause when one takes the buds (one or both) out. While this is a feature not often found at this price point, its absence was inconvenient.
Battery is another strong suit of the CMF Buds Neo. The buds promise 11 hours of listening time with ANC off, with 52 hours of total playback with ANC off, including the case. With ANC on, the numbers become 5 hours for the buds, and 30 hours with the case. We found the buds’ actual performance to be close to these numbers. With mixed use (ANC/ transparency mode on and off) at 70 percent volume, the buds easily lasted for around 9 hours. The buds also have a fast charging feature in which 10 minutes of charging gives one 5.5 hours of play time with ANC off . However, there is no cable in the box, which is a bit of a letdown.
CMF Buds Neo App: NothingX remains as clean and easy to use as ever
The NothingX app is the perfect accompaniment to the CMF Buds Neo – simple, clean and easy to use. We did have some trouble adding our Buds Neo to the app, but after a little struggle, the buds were added to the list of our other CMF devices. There is one main page, and you can scroll down to access all the functions and features. ANC, Spatial Audio, controls, bass enhancement, equalizer settings, low lag mode, dual connection, and firmware updates can all be accessed through the app. One also gets the exact charge percentage left in each earbud, although rather oddly, not that of the case. The app is easy to use and remains one of our favorites.
CMF Buds Neo Review Verdict: Superb value for the price
The CMF Buds Neo come with a price tag of Rs. 1,999, which is quite competitive for the performance and specs they offer. The similarly priced OnePlus Nord Buds 3r bring a comparable spec sheet, as do the Realme Buds T200 Lite, but both come with Bluetooth 5.4, marginally less playtime, and are not even close to the Buds Neo in the design department.
The CMF Buds Neo are near-perfect entry-level TWS options. Their audio, ANC, and battery performance give them an edge over the competition, and the distinct design is the cherry on this TWS cake. If you do not want to burn a hole in your pocket and still want a good pair of feature-packed TWS, the CMF Buds Neo are the perfect pick.
- Distinct design
- Enjoyable audio
- Good ANC
- Super call quality
- Very good companion app
- Good battery life
- Controls take some getting used to
- No charging cable in the box
- The white coloured case attracts scratches and smudges easily

Drivers on residential roads in Japan have been forced to take their foot off the accelerator, after the speed limit was slashed from 60km/h (37mph) to 30km/h in an attempt to reduce deaths and injuries among pedestrians on narrow urban streets.
The new limit, which went into effect on Tuesday, applies to residential roads with no centre line or maximum speed signs, media reports said.
Narrow roads with no centre lines or pavements are a common sight in crowded Japanese cities, with data indicating that children and older people are at particular risk of being involved in a fatal or serious accident.
The measures apply to about 870,000km of roads that are less than 5.5 metres wide and do not have centre lines or median strips, according to the Mainichi Shimbun. They account for about 70% of the country’s general roads, the newspaper said.
Authorities hopes the restrictions will address concerns that residential areas are not experiencing the same improvements in safety seen on larger roads.
While the overall number of deaths in traffic accidents is in decline – falling to a record low of 2,457 last year – those involving children and older people on residential roads has remained steady at about 300 a year since 2021, and rose for the first time in three years in 2025, according to the national police agency.
The introduction in 2011 of “zone 30” areas on a limited number of residential streets and along school routes resulted in a 30% reduction in fatalities and serious injuries, the Mainichi said.
Police agency data show that the mortality rate among pedestrians is less than 1% in accidents involving vehicles traveling at or below 30km/h, with the rate rising to 2.7% at speeds of 30-40km/h, and to 17.4% at 50-60km/h.
“We ask drivers to recognise that they need to take particular care on roads shared by vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists,” the police agency’s commissioner general, Yoshinobu Kusunoki, told reporters this week.

We’ll start this conference looking back on 2026 Washington Architecture by being honest: We have no idea what happened here. The snapshot of this planet that my comrades and I managed to obtain on our brief visit left us, if anything, more confused about Earth than we had been before. What follows are theories only.
All we know of 21st-century human political figure Donald J. Trump is what we can guess from the architectural record and a few bits of digital evidence. (Due to a misunderstanding, we ate most of the written records of this planet before figuring out that they contained information.) Was he a builder or a destroyer? There are also ruins of an arch—commemorating a triumph, but over what? Perhaps the successful defeat of 250 years of democracy, a system of rule that he despised?
Did he have access to the internet (a human technology that seems to have been primarily used for the sharing of pornography and misinformation)? Impossible to say. Some records suggest that a female of his species accessed the internet on his behalf. We don’t know his exact relation to this female, but we can observe that she was swift of foot and skilled at concealment in small enclosures, probably a trait admired by others. Were such relationships common? Did many human leaders consider it an honor to be chased by another human carrying a printer? (Did George Washington have a “Human Printer” of his own? Perhaps Benjamin Franklin fulfilled this role?)
Although other human figures enjoyed construction, Trump seemed to prefer the wrecking ball (what we would refer to as Grogon’s Tail) as a mode of expression. From a forensic analysis of these structures, we know that the Smashing of the Residence was first to take place, followed by the Desecration of the Pool.
Donald Trump seems to have smashed the Residence deliberately, as a warning to rivals. As his nestlings were at that time all mature and dwelling independently, such a gesture posed no danger to his young. Some papers we found suggested that there were plans to put something in the enormous hole, but these drawings are on an unlikely scale, and their suggested purpose is inconsistent. Ballroom? Bunker? No one can seem to agree, not even the plans themselves.
The situation of the pool is puzzling. We may never know why Donald Trump hated the pool (pond?) so much, but his action to strip it of its water, paint over its interior with a humiliating sealant, and fill it with a thick green algae speaks of immense disrespect. Had the pool or pond offended him? We know from the many banners he left bearing his visage around the city that he seems to have been incapable of smiling; a golden idol located in Florida represents him as having a slightly melted appearance. Perhaps glimpsing his reflection in the pond reminded him unpleasantly of these facts? Or were its ducks hostile to him? Some records show that even when the pool was drained of water, it was patrolled by an armed guard; what danger lurked in its shallows?
The structure with the giant head in it puzzles us most. We think this site on the Potomac may once have been used for entertainment and functioned as a kind of temple to the performing arts. Others suggest that it was an oversize dwelling place for mice. Some scholars believe that people really went inside the building and sat in red chairs while someone stood and bellowed in Italian. Perhaps this hall was used for punishment? Were wrongdoers subjected to the “tuba”?
Letters found near the site marking it “The Donald J. Trump and the John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts” suggest that the enormous bronze head may represent either Donald J. Trump or John F. Kennedy, in whose joint memory the center seems to have been erected. Who were these men? They must have loved the arts. Perhaps an American Harmodius and Aristogeiton? Curiously, we do not see them commemorated jointly in other locations.
Some scholars argue that Donald J. Trump was in fact alive at the time of the center’s commemoration, but other scholars reply that this claim is ludicrous—where else is there evidence of a Memorial Center constructed while its subject was still living? The same theory suggests that he added his name to the center decades after its construction, halted all the shows, removed the public artworks, and threatened to demolish it if his name was not kept on, but other scholars reply that smashing things unless you can write your name on them is hardly the behavior of a full-fledged adult. We truly don’t know what to make of this place. (Just for the record, though, we didn’t do the pyramids.)

Audacity 4 has been in the works for some time, and had its own mini controversy last year when an unfortunate redesigned logo started making the rounds. The final version of the new icon isn’t nearly as bad as the early rendition that was circulating last October. But more importantly, all the promised improvements to the self-proclaimed “world’s most popular audio editing and recording app” are here, turning Audacity from a free and capable but extremely clunky audio editor into a powerful modern tool.
Audacity 4 is a complete revamp of the ‘world’s most popular’ audio editor
Non-destructive editing, better clip management, and a new look bring the app into the modern age.
The biggest change is the move to a non-destructive editing workflow. That means you can trim a clip down, then recover the audio simply by dragging the edge of the clip back out if you change your mind. Clips can now overlap too, which means you can still paste in audio even if there isn’t enough space and adjust after, or just freely drag audio around the timeline. Previously, if you tried to drag a clip past another one in the timeline, it would just stop dead in its tracks. You’d instead have to cut and paste it to move it past any existing audio.
You can also split clips now to easily chop up and rearrange audio. The developers refreshed clip envelopes and the built-in effects, and added a home screen with revamped project organization. Audacity also got a dramatic facelift that brings it more in line with Muse’s other products like Muse Score and Audio.com, complete with customizable themes.
While Audacity has been a staple of many people’s toolkits since it debuted way back in 2000, it’s stayed stubbornly consistent in its design and layout as new features have been bolted on, sometimes clumsily. This big refresh to Audacity 4 brings it much closer to a modern digital audio workstation (DAW).

US job market rebounds as employers add 162,000 jobs and unemployment rate holds steady
The jobs report, released Friday by the Labor Department, may offer a welcome signal for President Donald Trump just two months prior to midterm elections
The U.S. employment landscape experienced a rebound in August, with business owners adding an unexpected 162,000 positions while the unemployment rate remained steady at 4.1 percent.
The employment figures, released Friday by the Labor Department, may offer a welcome signal for President Donald Trump just two months prior to midterm elections where economic performance is a central issue for voters.
The monthly expansion comfortably beat expectations of 65,000 additions predicted in a FactSet survey. Upward revisions by the Labor Department also painted a stronger picture, raising June and July employment figures by a combined 55,000. Companies actually added 21,000 jobs in July, reversing an initial government calculation of a 23,000 loss.
Meanwhile, the overall size of the American workforce—representing individuals currently working or seeking employment—rose by 683,000 last month after shrinking throughout June and July.
Enterprises continue to navigate a restricted supply of labor, driven by President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown along with an ongoing wave of retiring baby boomers. In response, some firms are turning toward digital technology to perform roles previously managed by human staff.
However, organizations remain hesitant to trim existing headcounts, granting the majority of American workers exceptional job stability while keeping overall jobless numbers depressed.
"It’s a very strange labor market,’’ David Kelly, chief global strategist at J.P. Morgan Asset Management, wrote in a commentary Monday.
The primary paradox facing analysts is that while new recruitment remains sluggish, job reductions remain exceptionally sparse.
Firms show little inclination to rapidly expand staff levels. Data from the Labor Department published Tuesday indicated that total gross recruitment—before factoring in departures or layoffs—dropped 5 percent to just under 5.1 million positions.
The U.S. economy no longer requires the same volume of monthly job creation as in previous years to prevent unemployment from escalating. President Donald Trump's immigration restrictions combined with baby boomer retirements mean fewer active job seekers are competing for openings, with over 1.3 million individuals leaving the active labor supply in the past 12 months.
Consequently, the monthly "break-even" target for new job creation—previously set at 155,000 over the 2023-2024 period—has fallen to near zero, according to research conducted by the Federal Reserve.
Rather than competing to recruit from a reduced pool of potential hires, "businesses are increasingly focused on boosting efficiency through technology and AI and increasingly seek to do more with their existing workforce,’’ EY-Parthenon economists Gregory Daco and Lydia Boussour wrote in a commentary this week.
Even without active recruitment initiatives, executive leadership remains unwilling to dismiss current employees, remembering the severe personnel deficits experienced after COVID-19 restrictions were lifted.
Thus, jobless figures stay low. Over the last year, initial applications for unemployment compensation—a key indicator of job cuts—have consistently hovered within a historically subdued bracket of 200,000 to 230,000.
This dynamic has created what financial analysts describe as a "no-hire, no-fire" economic environment, offering solid job security to existing staff while presenting substantial hurdles for younger applicants pursuing entry-level positions or out-of-work individuals trying to re-enter the labor market.

What will Jackson bring to Villa with Watkins set for exit?
- Published
Aston Villa have completed the signing of Nicolas Jackson in a deal worth up to £65m, with Ollie Watkins looking set to join Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal.
Unai Emery's Villa are undergoing a major overhaul this summer, with key players including Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne having already departed.
Jackson, 25, joins a number of new additions including Johan Manzambi, Joao Gomes, Zion Suzuki and Matteo Ruggeri.
That level of squad disruption was evident on the opening weekend, when Emery's side slumped to a 4-0 defeat at Brighton.
With Watkins, 30, unavailable and both Tammy Abraham and 17-year-old Brian Madjo injured, Villa started without a recognised centre-forward - Emiliano Buendia led the line.
The arrival of Jackson - who overtakes Manzambi to become Villa's record signing - from Chelsea gives Emery a specialist striker to work with.
It also looks set to coincide with the end of Watkins' six-year spell at Villa, during which he scored 108 goals in 278 games and became one of the defining players of the rise under Emery.
However, the stats suggest Jackson is not just a like-for-like replacement for the England international - he is a different type of number nine.
More involved, more shots - but a smaller sample
On the surface, Jackson's numbers at Bayern Munich last season compare favourably with those of Watkins at Villa.
The Senegal forward scored 11 goals and provided three assists in 1,320 minutes across all competitions, averaging 1.0 goal involvements per 90 minutes. Watkins recorded 21 goals and five assists in 3,837 minutes, an average of 0.6 per 90.
Jackson also generated more attacking opportunities. He averaged 3.8 shots per 90 compared with Watkins' 2.6, and 2.2 shots on target to 1.2.
His expected-goals (xG) figure was also higher, at 0.7 per 90 compared with 0.5, while he averaged 8.5 touches in the opposition box to Watkins' 5.6.
That fits a pattern which predates his spell in Germany. Among players with at least 5,000 Premier League minutes since January 2020, only Erling Haaland has registered a higher non-penalty xG figure per 90 than Jackson's 0.55.
Getting into scoring positions has rarely been Jackson's main problem - it is his ability to finish chances which has attracted scrutiny.
During his two Premier League seasons with Chelsea, he scored 14 goals from 18.7 xG in 2023-24 and 10 from 12.3 xG the following campaign.
Jackson has converted 18 of 61 big chances in England so far, although Watkins has also missed plenty of high-value opportunities (scoring 24 of 73 since joining Villa in 2020).
Interestingly, last season's numbers suggest the gap between them was negligible. Jackson converted 19.6% of his shots and 40.9% of his big chances, compared with 18.9% and 43.2% respectively for Watkins.
There is, however, an important caveat.
Watkins started 43 matches and played almost three times as many minutes. Jackson started only 15 of his 34 appearances, and Opta says his relatively limited, substitute-heavy sample could make some of his per-90 figures look stronger than they might over a full season.
Are Villa getting a different type of striker?
Both players were predominantly used as centre-forwards last season, making the comparison reasonably fair.
Watkins played 100% of his 3,837 minutes as a striker, with 92% coming as the central striker in Villa's 4-2-3-1.
Jackson spent 95% of his 1,320 minutes up front, with the remaining 5% on the left. At Bayern, 86% of his playing time came as the striker in a 4-2-3-1.
The similarity largely ends there. Jackson averaged 46.6 open-play touches per 90, compared with Watkins' 29.5, and completed almost twice as many passes - 24 per 90 to Watkins' 11.6.
He was also considerably more involved in creating and progressing attacks. Jackson averaged:
- 1.6 shot-ending carries per 90, compared with Watkins' 0.8
- 1.6 successful take-ons per 90, compared with 0.82
- 2.5 passes into the penalty area per 90, compared with 0.7.
Opta's touch maps reinforce the difference. Watkins' involvement was concentrated more heavily around the centre of the final third and penalty area, while Jackson received possession across a wider range of attacking zones.
Among a sample of 1,577 top-five European league strikers over the past 10 seasons, Jackson ranked in the 85th percentile for chances created, 77th for progressive carries and 73rd for touches.
Watkins ranked in the 28th, 53rd and eighth percentiles respectively. That points towards Villa moving from a relatively low-touch focal point to a forward who is more comfortable becoming involved in attacks earlier.
Greater intensity without the ball
There is another possible difference when Villa lose possession. Jackson averaged 34 high pressures per 90, slightly above Watkins' 31.4, but the distinction becomes clearer in where possession was recovered.
Jackson won the ball 2.7 times per 90, compared with Watkins' 1.8, and regained it in the final third 0.9 times per 90 to Watkins' 0.6.
His percentile for possession won in the attacking third was 88th among the Opta striker sample, compared with Watkins' 43rd.
The two were almost identical for runs in behind, Jackson averaging 13 per 90 and Watkins 12.7, although the Englishman made slightly more runs which finished inside the penalty area.
Watkins also offered more aerially, winning 1.2 aerial duels per 90 compared with Jackson's 0.7, and carried the ball more directly towards goal. So Jackson would not necessarily reproduce every aspect of the player he is replacing.
Why Emery believes he can unlock Jackson
Villa's interest also comes with an element of familiarity. Emery worked with Jackson at Villarreal, where the forward made 27 appearances under him, scoring three goals and providing three assists in 1,195 minutes.
Jackson has subsequently credited Emery with transforming his understanding of the game.
"Unai taught me everything about football," he said,
Jackson has explained that, when he arrived from Senegal, he possessed natural dribbling ability but had much less understanding of how and when to move.
Emery helped turn that instinctive talent into a more structured game.
Jackson's development accelerated after Emery left Villarreal. During the 2022-23 La Liga season he produced 0.56 non-penalty xG plus xA per 90, a rate bettered by only seven players with at least 1,500 minutes, all representing Barcelona, Real Madrid or Atletico Madrid.
Jackson's ability to carry the ball was already evident too. Ten of his league goal involvements followed carries, fewer only than Vinicius Jr, despite Jackson playing substantially fewer minutes.
Chelsea subsequently signed him in 2023. He scored 30 goals and supplied 12 assists in 81 appearances for the club before spending last season on loan at Bayern.
His time in Munich was complicated by circumstances rather than simply performance.
Bayern's obligation to buy would have been triggered if he reached a demanding appearance threshold, but Harry Kane remained fit and prolific, while the displays of Luis Diaz and Michael Olise limited opportunities elsewhere across the frontline.
Jackson still produced 11 goals across all competitions, and only Kane recorded a better rate of open-play Bundesliga goals per 90.
Bayern coach Vincent Kompany publicly defended him when criticism resurfaced, pointing to the quality of the forwards ahead of him and saying Jackson had trained and performed well.
A replacement - but not necessarily a replica
Watkins has provided Villa with reliability, running power and goals throughout one of the club's most successful periods of the modern era.
Jackson arrives with a different profile. He is five years younger, gets more touches, carries the ball more frequently, creates more for others and, in limited minutes last season, generated shots and high-quality chances at an impressive rate.
There remain questions around whether those per-90 numbers would survive a heavier workload, while his finishing record at Chelsea explains why doubts have followed him.
But Villa are not buying an unknown quantity. Emery has coached Jackson before, knows the qualities he wants to develop and would be replacing a 30-year-old striker with a 25-year-old whose underlying numbers suggest there may still be considerable room to improve.
If Jackson joins and Watkins does depart, the Europa League winners will be doing more than just changing their centre-forwards.
They will be changing the way their number nine plays.

Defence planners working with Nato fear that if war broke out with Russia, Europe could not currently sustain a prolonged war of attrition owing to a public lack of war readiness, a conference on the future of European military coordination heard this week.
The pessimism reflects concern that Russia may be winning a so-called hybrid war with Europe, weakening the options available to Nato war planners in the event of military conflict.
The surge in support for the populist forces in Europe’s main military states is also endangering proposals for a group of five European countries, including the UK, to take on a new coordination role as the US prepares to reduce its commitments to the conventional defence of Europe.
Defence officials, speaking at a forum convened by the Munich Security Conference (MSC), the leading security foundation, said the European public may not have the appetite for a prolonged war, requiring Nato to focus its plans on a relatively quick conflict.
One recent British cabinet member admitted the west had been “crap” at educating its public about the scale of the hybrid conflict with Russia. Another UK diplomat claimed successive British prime ministers had done nothing to explain the scale of the threat.
They said this had left ministers locked in an unenviable task of persuading unprepared voters to cut welfare spending to fund defence. “The level of the debate has been at that of a kindergarten,” the UK diplomat admitted.
The private criticism has been fuelled by the UK government’s inability to adopt a call in its 2025 strategic defence review to launch a national conversation on the scale of the security threat facing Europe and to build national resilience.
A second diplomat said the collapse of the cold war dividing line with Russia had left Moscow free to exploit the anxieties of European publics on the left and the right. The remarks reveal a wider concern in senior European politicians that they may be losing the so-called hybrid war with Russia, and this may be reflected in rightwing populist surges next year in Poland, France and Italy.
Most populist parties, including Germany’s Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), are sympathetic to Russia and want an end to the Ukraine conflict.
The MSC discussion – held under rules forbidding identification of the speaker – was given added urgency by the German government this week blaming Russia for an attempted drone attack on Leipzig airport last month.
One of the suspected culprits in the attack on 4 August, where an armed drone exploded, has been identified as a Belarusian citizen with a Russian passport who appears to have entered Europe using an Italian tourist visa.
The MSC, an independent but influential foundation, has been promoting the idea of the five main European military powers working much more closely: one means of bringing the UK, outside the EU, to the centre of European defence planning.
Decisions in Washington on its troop deployments that could effectively leave Europe in charge of its own conventional defences are expected in the next few months. But the scale of hybrid war and the potential impact of next year’s elections, as well as the surge by the AfD in Germany, on plans for a stronger European defence coordination was described at the conference as “the elephant in the room”.
One proposal is for the EU to publish a collective statement on the Russian threat that the populist forces would be challenged to accept or decline.
The E5 group of European defence ministers already meet regularly, but they are at the early stages of agreeing of how to jointly procure capabilities such as integrated air and missile defence, deep precision strike and space-based early warning systems that are all currently provided mostly by the US.
“Europe is stagnating at a time when the external threats were assuming a dimension which is really very serious. These are really huge and existential challenges requiring greater integration in defence,” said Wolfgang Ischinger, the chair of the MSC.
He argued the E5 grouping offers a way of including all the European countries with substantial defence industrial capacity and may later be able to incorporate Ukraine in the context of a truce since Kyiv now has the largest and strongest army in Europe.
Advocates of the E5 insist it will neither duplicate nor underline Nato, but fears were expressed that the US would nevertheless block a stronger European pillar inside Nato. “The US are better at talking about burden shifting than power sharing,” said one diplomat.
Italy is one of the E5 states most concerned about the impact of Russia’s hybrid warfare on its domestic politics as Giorgia Meloni’s rightwing administration – which has governed more moderately than many expected, and cultivated a pro-Ukraine image abroad – becomes its longest-running since the second world war.
The Italian foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, warned Italy was suffering daily cyber-attacks, adding it was not immune from potential Russian interference in next year’s national elections, the first time an Italian politicians has warned the election may be manipulated.
“There are many ways to wage hybrid warfare, it is not done using bombs, planes or tanks,” the minister said.
Italy’s defence minister, Guido Crosetto, one of Meloni’s closest political allies, has said it was stupid not to recognise the level of Russian interference.
He warned this summer at the Nato summit in Ankara: “We don’t have the antibodies and we’re penetrable: analyse bots and you’ll see it. The increase occurred thanks to social media.”
His doubts have grown given Moscow’s ability to operate across so many domains, including social media, AI, cybersecurity, databases and critical infrastructure. On Tuesday, he said the Russian threat was growing all the time.
Crosetto also said he recognises Russia is exploiting real problems such as low wages, and so attributing government unpopularity to Russian disinformation risks misidentifying a malaise afflicting western societies, including a general weariness with the cost of the war in Ukraine,
In Italy, Roberto Vannacci, the leader of the far-right Futuro Nazionale who has challenged the stability of Meloni’s coalition, is widely seen as the most probable carrier of the Russian message in the coming election, that could come as early as April.
Speaking before the investigation into whether his party represents a revival of fascism, Vannacci gloried in the criticism. “Just discovered that I am a ‘Manchurian candidate’ sent by the Russian federation to complain about the unaffordable petrol prices in my country Italy,” he said. “Forgive me, but I still find it hard to accept the idea that dissent from Brussels’ orthodoxy is now, in practical terms, tantamount to disloyalty towards the west.”
In an attempt to shift perceptions so Ukraine is seen not as a financial burden but rather as teaching Europe modern warfare, Crosetto has recruited the former Ukraine defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov as his unpaid adviser for innovation. Ischinger praised the decision, describing Ukraine as possessing the best equipped and most modern army in Europe.
In Ukraine, 200,000 drones are being built each month, with the goal of producing more than 7m by 2026. To support this growth, 500 small and medium-sized companies have sprung up, assembling drones even in small workshops, using mostly Chinese components.

For many Europeans, this summer’s heat was a powerful reminder of the damage climate change has wrought — from illness and devastated crops to high energy bills. For Andrew Austin, a 34-year-old homeowner in Shropshire, England, the stubbornly high temperatures were a chance to make some money.
Power demand was rising as London crossed 34 degrees Celsius on June 24. Energy prices spiked as the sun set and solar panels across the U.K. stopped generating electricity. That’s when Austin knew he could take advantage of his 200 kilowatt-hour home battery, which he had charged up using cheap power from the grid during the daytime. He sold the power back to the grid for £60 ($82) from 4 p.m. to 9 p.m. In just a few hours, Austin had earned about as much as an apartment dweller would typically pay for electricity every month.
All this happened without Austin having to press a single button. He has set up a computer to conduct this energy trading while he goes about his life as normal. The computer downloads electricity prices for every 30-minute period from his utility Octopus Energy, which publishes them at 4 p.m. each day. That allows him to know when electricity will be cheap to charge his batteries, and when power prices on the grid are high, the computer sells it back to the grid.

Myanmar military head visits Vietnam to normalize relations
BANGKOK — The leader of Myanmar's military-backed government arrived Friday in Vietnam for talks with Vietnamese leaders in his latest effort to normalize relations with other Southeast Asian countries and attract foreign investment.
Min Aung Hlaing has stepped up his diplomatic engagements since he was sworn in as president in April following an election that critics say was designed to cement the military's hold on power.
The outreach is part of an attempt to rebuild regional ties that deteriorated after Min Aung Hlaing ousted Aung San Suu Kyi's government in February 2021 while serving as army chief.
Friday's trip marks Min Aung Hlaing's third visit to an Association of Southeast Asian Nations member state as he seeks to restore his standing within the 11-member bloc, to which Myanmar and Vietnam belong.
Min Aung Hlaing faced years of diplomatic isolation following his 2021 takeover and was barred from top-level ASEAN meetings for failing to comply with a peace plan for Myanmar adopted by the bloc in April 2021.
He has traveled to India, China, Laos, Thailand and most recently Kazakhstan, Belarus and Russia, where he met with leaders and sought to attract foreign investment through business forums.
State-run MRTV television said Min Aung Hlaing landed at Noi Bai International Airport in Vietnam's capital, Hanoi, at noon.
He is expected to meet during his three-day visit with Vietnamese President To Lam and other senior officials and attend a business forum with members of his Cabinet.
Vietnam has maintained longstanding military ties with Myanmar, including defense cooperation and the involvement of Viettel, Vietnam's military-run telecommunications group, in Mytel, one of Myanmar's major telecom operators.
Economic ties, however, have weakened, with bilateral trade falling from $853 million in 2020 to $590 million in 2025 and $335 million in the first half of 2026, figures Min Aung Hlaing shared with Vietnam's Foreign Minister Le Hoai Trung when they met in Myanmar in late August, according to Vietnam's foreign ministry.
Western governments have shunned and sanctioned Min Aung Hlaing and his associates for overthrowing Suu Kyi's government and for serious human rights violations committed since. The military's deadly crackdown on protests helped trigger a nationwide armed resistance movement and a bloody civil war.

US envoys arrive in Moscow ahead of Ukraine talks
- Published
Two of US President Donald Trump's top envoys have arrived in Moscow ahead of a weekend of talks aimed at accelerating efforts to end the war in Ukraine.
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were due in the Russian capital on Saturday, where they will hold talks before travelling to Kyiv on Sunday for discussions with Ukraine.
Trump told reporters on Friday the pair were "bringing with them a proposal to end the war". So far, efforts from the US and its allies to broker a peace deal have failed to deliver a breakthrough.
US news outlet Axios reported the US envoys would separately meet both Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Judge ready to declare mistrial in Lindsay Clancy case but allows last-minute Hail Mary by defense
The jury in Lindsay Clancy's trial has repeatedly told the judge that they were deadlocked and could not come to a verdict
The judge in Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial says he’s ready to declare a mistrial but allowed her defense attorney a last-minute “Hail Mary” before doing so.
Judge William Sullivan said in court that he saw no choice but to declare a mistrial after receiving a note from the jury Friday, stating, “With a heavy heart, we report we cannot come to a unanimous decision."
The jury was about to walk back into the courtroom for his ruling when Clancy's defense lawyer, Kevin Reddington, asked for a chance to file an emergency appeal with the Supreme Judicial Court.
In a stunning development, the judge allowed Reddington one hour to get a stay from the Supreme Judicial Court. The mistrial ruling is now on hold.
Jurors have deliberated for seven days and told the judge three times that they have been unable to reach a unanimous verdict.
If the judge declares a mistrial, prosecutors must decide whether to retry the case, offer a plea deal, or drop the charges.
A conviction could mean life in prison for Clancy, while an acquittal might lead to confinement in a mental health facility.
Over a five-week trial, the jury heard testimony from doctors, first responders, relatives and even Clancy’s former husband. The jurors were tasked with determining whether she should be held criminally responsible for killing her three young children at her Massachusetts home in 2023.
Both sides agree Clancy did it. But her attorneys argued the former labor and delivery nurse was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time, and that poor mental healthcare exacerbated her condition. Prosecutors argued she intentionally planned the killings.
Clancy's former husband made anguished 911 call
Clancy's former husband, Patrick Clancy, was first to take the stand at trial. In emotional testimony, he described the day he found his wife after she tried to kill herself.
Lindsay Clancy had sent him out to get takeout food and medication for their daughter, which prosecutors argue was an excuse to get him out of the house.
He came home to find the house unusually silent, before finding blood throughout the main bedroom and a window open.
Jurors listened to the 911 call Patrick Clancy made after finding his wife outside in the snow. Clancy can be heard speaking with his wife, then tells the dispatcher he’s going to check on the children.
Moments later, he howls and cries after finding his children in the basement. The confused dispatcher repeatedly asks what happened.
“She killed the kids!” he yells.
Everyone knew Clancy was struggling
Clancy's mother, mother-in-law, sister, friends and co-workers testified that Clancy struggled with her mental health after giving birth to Callan, the youngest of her three children.
Clancy's mother-in-law, Susan Clancy, said she and her former daughter-in-law were close. Both worked as labor and delivery nurses. She described Lindsay as a wonderful mother.
But Susan Clancy testified that Lindsay had become anxious, paranoid and suicidal, and that the psychiatric care she was getting wasn't helping.
“She felt unwell. She had insomnia. She was losing her appetite. She was very anxious and sad,” Susan Clancy said. “She was begging for help.”
Lindsay Clancy’s mother, Paula Musgrove, testified that her daughter was scared of sleeping alone, became paranoid and believed the medications she was taking “were destroying her mind.”
“Mom, will you please come up and stay with me for a bit? I’m really sick. Something is wrong,” Clancy wrote in an October 2022 text message that Paula Musgrove read in court.
“I had horrible insomnia all night, and I just don’t know how I am going to get through the day. … It’s just really scary, and I don’t want to be alone.”
The defense questioned the quality of Clancy's medical care
Clancy saw several doctors about her declining mental health, and eventually checked herself in to a psychiatric hospital. Her lawyer, Kevin Reddington, argued that she was misdiagnosed and overmedicated.
As he cross-examined one of her psychiatrists, Dr. Jennifer Tufts, Reddington questioned her expertise, prescribing decisions and use of 25-minute video appointments with limited time for talk therapy. At one point, Reddington implied that Tufts was a box-checking “robot.”
“What did you do? You had a woman who was telling you she felt hopeless,” he asked as they discussed an appointment about two months before the killings.
“I told her that this was something we could address, that there was hope, that there are treatments, that there are different types of programs,” Tufts said, “so she knew that she still had options and a reason to hope.”
Clancy said she heard a voice telling her to kill
Paul Zeizel, a clinical and forensic psychologist who visited Lindsay Clancy in the hospital after she killed the children, testified that he overheard her saying that a disembodied male voice had told her she had no choice but to kill her children and then herself. Zeizel said he believed Clancy wasn't responsible for her actions because of her deep mental illness.
Prosecutors called a rebuttal witness, forensic psychologist Kirk Heilbrun, who said he didn’t believe Clancy had hallucinated voices.
“One of the things that she said when I asked about what happened, is that in the course of strangling each child, she said, ‘Go to God, baby. Go to God,’” he said. “That was part of her expectation that she and the children would be together in heaven with God.”
Dr. Gregory Saathoff, a senior psychiatrist for the FBI’s Behavioral Analysis Unit, testified for prosecutors that Clancy “had the capacity to know right from wrong.”
The lawyers got the last word
After testimony was complete, each side got about an hour to make their closing argument to the jury.
Reddington showed the jury a photograph of the Clancy family, looking happy, and a second one of Lindsay Clancy in the hospital.
“How does this turn into this?" Reddington asked. “How? Because of the damn medicine and the lousy medical care that she got.”
Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague said criticizing the mental health system was “a distraction.” She said Clancy chose to kill her children because doing so would make it easier to kill herself.
“She was depressed. She was exhausted. She was done. She didn’t want to try anymore. She felt damaged,” Sprague said. “But those kids, those kids were her protective factor. Those kids were keeping her from ending her misery.”

Frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI all experienced rare outages on Thursday morning, creating downtime for their corresponding AI chatbots. SpaceX, xAI’s parent company, said on Thursday afternoon that the issues with Grok resulted from “an outage at our Memphis compute center this morning.”
The issues initially appeared to be linked because they coincided—perhaps the result of a shared third-party service provider—but neither OpenAI nor Anthropic cited an external source in comments to WIRED on Thursday. SpaceX, xAI’s parent company, did not respond to WIRED’s request for comment. But the company said as part of its public comments on Thursday: “We’d also like to apologize to our impacted compute partners.” Anthropic and xAI announced a “compute partnership” with SpaceX in May.
OpenAI spokesperson Kathleen Chaykowski tells WIRED: “A routing error starting around 7:43 am PT on Thursday, September 3, made ChatGPT and Codex unavailable for some users across platforms. As of about 8:17 am PT on Thursday, a solution was successfully implemented and is continuing to be monitored.”
Anthropic declined to comment on the episode. The company began alerting about a “partial outage” at 6:23 am PT on Thursday that involved “elevated errors on requests to Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Opus 5.” Shortly after, the company said it had “identified the cause” and that “a fix has been deployed.” The company marked the issue as resolved by 9:16 am PT. Claude Sonnet 5 seemed to briefly have similar issues shortly after 9 am PT.
xAI reported Grok outages across all of its platforms and services beginning at 6:30 am PT when the company posted “investigating outage” on its service status page. “Grok is experiencing issues. We are working on restoring service as quickly as possible,” the page said. At 10:05 am PT the episode was marked complete. “We have resolved the situation, and traffic is healthy again,” the company wrote.
There were scattered reports of a possible Google Gemini outage on Thursday morning as well, but the company did not confirm this or record any incidents on its service status dashboard. Google did not respond to WIRED’s request for comment ahead of publication.
Typically, multiple outages in the same sector at the same time would point to a cloud provider, content delivery network, or other third-party vendor having issues affecting multiple customers. But OpenAI and Anthropic did not point to a potential shared cause, and major players in the internet infrastructure space—including Cloudflare, Amazon Web Services, and Microsoft Azure—did not report outages on Thursday.

Kenya's Ruto orders Indian company Tata Chemicals to leave the country
Kenya's President William Ruto has directed Tata Chemicals to leave the country, accusing the company of failing to generate economic impact
NAIROBI, Kenya -- NAIROBI, Kenya (AP) — Kenya's President William Ruto on Friday directed Tata Chemicals to leave the country, saying the Indian company failed to generate any economic impact in one of Kenya's most important export sectors.
Tata Chemicals produces soda ash from Lake Magadi that is used in the manufacture of glass, soaps and detergents. Kenya's exports of soda ash came to 254,779 tons, valued at $56.9 million, in the year to July 2025, according to government data.
The company should “pack and leave” in place of a new investor, Ruto said at a public rally on Thursday.
Tata Chemicals Magadi Limited has been in Kenya since 2005. Its operations were suspended by Kenya's ministry of mining in July, pending a “compliance review."
The company’s departure from Kenya could lead to job losses and significant loss of revenue.
Ruto said while soda ash from Lake Magadi is capable of changing Kenya for the better, the Indian company has “not built anything in Kajiado," the county where the lake is located. “They have not built any factory or employed people,” he said.

“I told them to pack and leave. They have been taking our resources and shipping them to India. We will bring a new company and the condition set is they must build a glass factory here," the Kenyan leader added.

- The claim that Canada assisted China in avoiding U.S. tariffs by reselling Chinese steel as Canadian is still under investigation.
- U.S. businesses and the U.S. government have accused Canadian companies of acting as a "backdoor" funneling Chinese steel into the United States. President Donald Trump's administration also has accused Canada of being one of China's "biggest enablers" in efforts to avoid tariffs in general.
- In May, the Department of Justice reached a settlement with two Canadian companies accused of falsely labeling Chinese steel as Canadian to avoid customs duties. However, the companies did not admit fault as part of the settlement.
- Some trade experts have expressed skepticism that Canada is enabling Chinese efforts to avoid tariffs on steel. Canada's government also has enacted a number of measures in an attempt to prevent Chinese steel from flooding the Canadian market.
- We have not rated this claim due to a lack of verifiable evidence. We reached out to offices of the U.S. and Canadian trade representatives and will update this story if we hear back.
In the fall and summer of 2026, social media users claimed that Canada resold Chinese steel as Canadian to help China avoid U.S. tariffs.
The rumor spread on Facebook and X (screenshot, screenshot). Snopes readers also contacted us to investigate its legitimacy.
It is true that American businesses have accused Canadian companies — not the country's government — of skirting tariffs by selling Chinese goods, including steel, as Canadian. In an August report, Trump's administration also accused Canada of being one of "China's biggest enablers" in helping evade tariffs in general through "transshipment," or the shipment of goods from one country to another via a stop in yet another country.
In May, the Department of Justice reached a $19 million settlement with two Canadian companies over allegations that they "knowingly and improperly" failed to pay duties owed on steel manufactured in European and Asian countries, including China. The defendants denied the allegations and the settlement is not an admission of fault, but it also does not mean the United States' allegations were unfounded, according to the court documents (Page 2).
Snopes relies on independent verification and primary evidence for all of our conclusions. As of this writing, the courts have not determined that any Canadian company or government official has attempted to evade tariffs or help China avoid tariffs through this supposed scheme. Furthermore, there is not enough publicly available evidence that such a scheme has happened or is happening. As such, we have not rated this claim.
We reached out to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Canada's trade minister for the U.S., Dominc LeBlanc, for more information and await a response.
It is also worth noting that the claims connected these allegations to the breakdown in U.S.-Canada trade talks in late summer 2026. That may be because Greer reportedly raised concerns to Canadian officials about the transshipment of Chinese steel through countries Canada is seeking new free-trade deals with.
Here's what we know about the allegations:
US businesses accuse Canadian firms of avoiding tariffs
In December 2025, American industry leaders accused Canadian and Mexican firms of using cheap Chinese materials in ways that undercut U.S. businesses during a public hearing on the future of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade 
For example, here's what Brandon Farris, vice president of the Steel Manufacturers Association, said, according to Page 135 of the official transcript for the Dec. 4, 2025 hearing:
Some producers of steel-intensive goods in both countries continue to rely on steel sourced from non-market, excess capacity nations such as China. From 2020 to 2024, Mexico's steel imports from China rose by 59 percent, while Canada's increased by nearly 75 percent. Just as Canada and Mexico have experienced rising imports from countries with chronic excess steel capacity, the U.S. has faced its own surge of steel products from both neighbors.
Michael Salmon, CEO of Specialty Steel Works in Indiana, said that "China in particular continues to use Mexico as back door access to key U.S. markets, including steel" (Page 139). And Bob Wahlin, CEO of Stoughton Trailers, an American trailer manufacturer, said the United States must "close loopholes in the agreement" allowing "highly subsidized" Chinese steel to "enter the U.S. market from Canada and Mexico" (Page 244).
DOJ, US government accusations against Canada
The best publicly available evidence that at least some Canadian firms may be skirting tariffs on Chinese steel appears to be the previously mentioned Department of Justice settlement with two Canadian companies, Farjess and Royal Canadian Steel.
According to the Justice Department's complaint, the same people oversee Royal Canadian Steel and Farjess. Royal Canadian Steel imported steel into Canada and supplied that steel to Farjess (PDF pages 4 and 5).
The DOJ alleged that Farjess and/or Royal Canadian Steel personnel removed labels on steel referencing a Chinese company in order to conceal the origin of the steel from customs officials (PDF pages 13 to 15). Allegedly, the companies replaced the Chinese labels with their own. Evidence submitted in court included scans of those labels (see Exhibits 7 and 8).
While this scheme may have helped Chinese companies avoid tariffs, the Justice Department's allegations focused on the benefits to the two Canadian firms — specifically, that they experienced "windfall profits" from the allegedly fraudulent activity (PDF Page 22).
Skepticism of US claims and Canada's response
CBC reported in 2025 that Eric Miller, an expert on Canada-U.S. trade policy with the Canadian Global Affairs Institute, said Canada is "nowhere near as much of a back door for Chinese steel as the American companies make it out to be."
Miller reportedly said Canada is "quite militant" about prevention of Chinese transshipment because it wants to protect its own access to the U.S. market.
"Any objective look at Canada's track record would say that repeatedly over the last decade, Canada has seriously put in place measures to try to control imports of Chinese steel," the CBC quoted Miller as saying.
Indeed, in July 2025, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced measures to restrict and reduce foreign steel from entering the Canadian market amid fears from Canada's steel industry that it would be overwhelmed by an influx of Chinese steel newly subject to U.S. tariffs.

A SAP executive says the "pendulum will swing back" from the SaaSpocalypse.
Like many software companies, the German software giant has seen its stock hit hard over the past year amid competition from AI tools. This stock sell-off of software-as-a-service (SaaS) companies, known as the SaaSpocalypse, has hit companies like Salesforce, SAP, and Workday as Anthropic and OpenAI have introduced tools that could threaten their businesses.
SAP's stock has been down about 20% over the past year, though it's been on an upward trend over the past month.
When SAP reported its earnings in late July, investors responded positively to the company's cloud-led growth and advances in its business AI. Jan Gilg, SAP's global president of customer success and Americas, told Business Insider that the sell-off was "a bit of an overreaction on the entire industry."
"As usual, I feel the pendulum will swing back," Gilg said. "There will be users. There will be losers and winners. I truly believe SAP will be on the side of the winners."
To get on the winning side, Gilg says SAP has been reinventing itself with AI, investing in its data capabilities, and changing its pricing models.
"Everybody has AI on the agenda right now," Gilg said.
SAP bounces back from the SaaSpocalypse
SAP's stock has jumped roughly 40% since it reported earnings in late July.
There's a reason for that, Gilg says. SAP isn't easily replaceable through a vibe-coded tool, though Gilg does expect companies to leverage AI to build software much faster. Internally, SAP has also used AI to improve its output and build its own software, and it sees AI as an opportunity to improve its tools for customers.
"It's really multifaceted. On the one side, there was the idea that customers will vibe code their software themselves rather than buying packaged software. We don't see that frankly," Gilg said. "We don't see that, especially for mission-critical purposes. It's not just about features and functions. It's about auditability, governance, and the maintenance of the software."
While Gilg says he hasn't seen customers replacing SAP software, he has seen competition over tech budgets—especially with token spending, or how companies pay for AI. SAP has a "good position" for this because customers rely on SAP data to run their business processes and can demonstrate its value, Gilg said.
"Customers are seeing token costs go through the roof already," Gilg said. "How do you measure and control that, and how do you show an outcome for that? Budgets won't necessarily increase. It will still have to come from somewhere. Therefore, the scrutiny will become much, much bigger."
SAP is competing more with Palantir
Lately, Gilg has been focusing on explaining to customers how they can benefit from AI and what SAP can offer. Customers have spent a lot of money on AI, though many haven't seen the business outcomes, profit, or productivity gains they're looking for.
"Customers have not yet seen the benefit of AI," Gilg said. "That is certainly something they are digging deeper into now."
To address that, SAP built its first foundational model, Tabular AI, which can help make predictions based on business data. In the future, Gilg expects people to interact with SAP products through natural language and voice.
SAP has also been investing in its ontology capabilities to allow customers to audit their systems and work with AI agents to help make decisions. Ontology is a favorite Palantir buzzword, and these capabilities put SAP in more direct competition with the AI data company.
While SAP competes with Palantir, they also partner to move data between systems. SAP says its advantage over rivals is its data from over 10,000 customers, which allows it to build more useful capabilities.
"We do see new players out there from Anthropic, OpenAI, Palantir, and so on," Gilg said. "That's going to be the battlefield of the future."
Internally, SAP uses AI across departments such as finance, human resources, and more. For example, employees can use an internal chatbot to ask questions or AI tools to write code. Sales employees can use AI to help with customer briefings or to study markets.
"We are definitely pivoting the company all in on AI," Gilg said. "We're doing this in a position of strength. Frankly, it's an evolution for us as well."
SAP is overhauling how it charges for AI
Gilg says AI will help SAP grow as it changes its business model. For example, it's moving from some subscription models to consumption-based models, meaning customers pay for what they use. The market has been shifting toward this pricing model, especially as high AI usage can drive up costs.
"What outcome are they driving?" Gilg said. "That's how we charge the consumption of those agents, which is very transparent to customers. Also, it's much easier to justify why they would actually pay for it. That's the current model many are following."
SAP still has a large subscription business, and many large customers use a hybrid model between subscription and consumption-based pricing.
More SaaS acquisitions could be coming
This year, SAP acquired Prior Labs, Reltio, and Dremio to boost its AI and data capabilities. Across the industry, Gilg expects to see a wave of acquisitions, especially with more AI-native startups and talent coming out of these companies.
"There's going to be a camp of losers and winners," Gilg said. "We have seen valuations go down quite significantly. That's an opportunity and interest for companies like that to look at wide spaces."
Gilg says SAP will also consider this if it makes sense for its business, though it would avoid companies that can be easily replaced by AI. If it's costly and time-consuming to switch from that software, customers are less likely to replace it with an AI-built application, Gilg said.
"I do see that there will certainly be a level of consolidation from my perspective, especially with vendors focused on single products," Gilg said. "Maybe niche areas, like legal contract management. Those are spaces that probably will be disrupted quite significantly."

Hamilton NHL prospect Matthew Mayich 'needs a miracle' after training collapse, family lawyer says
Lawyer for St. Louis Blues draftee calls for investigation into 'brutal' workout at Arizona State University
Hamilton-born NHL prospect Matthew Mayich "needs a miracle" after being hospitalized following a training incident at Arizona State University last month, his family's lawyer has said.
Attorney Rob Carey spoke to CBC Hamilton on behalf of Mayich's family on Friday, saying the 21-year-old's parents, who live in Hamilton's Stoney Creek area, are staying near the hospital to be with their son each day.
"They really appreciate the love and the prayers and the support they've received from their Canadian friends," the partner with U.S. law firm Hagens Berman Sobol Shapiro LLP said.
The St. Louis Blues draft pick collapsed following a morning workout at Arizona State University (ASU), Carey said. He said Mayich suffered exertional heatstroke causing a lack of oxygen to the brain.
A report in the journal BMJ Medicine describes exertional heatstroke as "the third leading cause of mortality in athletes during physical activity." It says data indicate mortality rates of about 27 per cent, with long-term negative health consequences for survivors.
University says senior vice-president reviewing incident
ASU confirmed a student on the hockey team collapsed during an Aug. 20 training session but has not named them, citing privacy obligations.
"The morning outdoor workout was a team event at which coaches and training staff were present along with a third party who had previously worked with the ASU Hockey team," the university said in a Sept. 3 statement.
ASU vice-president James Rund is leading a review, the school said, looking at "the workout and related university policies, procedures and training protocols."
The review will be conducted in a manner respectful of "the student-athlete, his family, his teammates and ASU’s privacy obligations," ASU said.
Mayich endured 'brutal' workout: lawyer
The university has been "tight-lipped" about what occurred, Carey said, but based on his own investigation, he believes Mayich endured a "military-style, brutal, grueling workout," with no breaks and no water for over an hour.
"You have an elite NHL-drafted athlete showing up on the first coach-led workout, the very first day the team could organize formally, and he left the field with no chance of recovery," Carey said. "Obviously there's something wrong."
When Mayich collapsed, the lawyer said that no one immediately immersed him in cool water, contrary to best practices for treating heat stroke.
It was about 31 C in Tempe, a college town just east of Phoenix, as of 7:51 a.m. on Aug. 20, according to Weather Underground. University police received a call about the hockey player's collapse around 8:30 a.m., ASU said.
CBC asked ASU to respond to Carey's allegations and to provide details about its own investigation.
A spokesperson said they had no further information beyond the Sept. 3 statement.
The university has guidelines for heat illness, as well as for for how third parties interact with ASU athletes, the statement said.
Questions about the workout are part of ASU's review, it added.
Family's questions unanswered
"The goal right now is just to get evidence about what happened," Carey said. "We don't know why [the workout] was set up, who set it up, what was really designed for the day, what safety precautions were taken, and who made a decision not to have safety precautions ready."
The family wants a fair and complete investigation, involving witness interviews, security video and digital communications, he said.
"If it's not happening, then either we need a proper police department to investigate it or we will do it when we have the ability with a civil lawsuit," Carey said.
CBC asked the University of Arizona Police Department if it's investigating but did not receive a response.
Mayich mentored younger players in Hamilton
Mayich played minor hockey with the Hamilton Huskies between 2016 and 2020 then with the Ottawa 67's before the St. Louis Blues drafted the defenceman in the sixth round of the 2023 NHL draft.
During his six seasons with the Huskies and one as a member of the Hamilton Jr. Bulldogs, Mayich established "himself as a tremendous hockey player and, more importantly, an outstanding person both on and off the ice," the Hamilton Steel Hockey Club, formerly the Huskies, said.
The statement was sent to CBC Hamilton on behalf of the organization, former Huskies president Mike Spadafora and former Huskies head coach Chris Travale. Spadafora is currently the councillor for Hamilton's Ward 14, running for re-election.
"Without fail, whenever [Mayich] is asked, he comes back every year to speak and skate with a new crop of young kids," Travale said. "His message is always about so much more than hockey — it’s about relationships, friendships, and the experiences you have along the hockey journey.
"From everyone at Hamilton Steel Hockey Club, the Hamilton Huskies family, Hamilton Jr. Bulldogs and the Hamilton hockey community — Matthew remains in our thoughts and prayers, and our hearts are with him and the entire Mayich family."

Suspect killed his girlfriend and her kids after finding out she cheated on him with an ex, cops say
Both a teenage girl and a boy under 10-years-of-age were pronounced dead at the scene
A Nevada man killed his girlfriend and two children after finding out that she cheated on him with an ex, police say.
Juan Carlos Orona, 29, turned himself in just around 7 p.m. Tuesday in connection to the case. When officers arrived at a Las Vegas address provided by Orona, they discovered the bodies of an adult woman, a teenage girl and a boy under 10 years of age.
All had suffered gunshot wounds and were pronounced dead at the scene, the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department confirmed in a statement.
Orona told police that he confronted his girlfriend, Nohani Flores-Osuna, at her apartment. According to an arrest report obtained by KLAS, he had been dating Flores-Osuna for three to six months and was staying at the home.
The suspect told Flores-Osuna that he saw her vehicle near her ex-boyfriend’s car. The ex was identified in the report only as “Henry.”
“Juan confirmed he confronted Nohani about infidelity with Henry and she confirmed she had been having sexual relations with Henry, and he was better in bed than Juan,” the report reads.
The report continues, “After hearing this, Juan stated he blacked out, and when he came to, he was holding his Glock 9MM handgun in the bathroom, and Nohani and her children’s bodies were on the ground.”
The arrest report revealed that Orona’s father drove him to Southeast Area Command and that the suspect could not remember how the shooting unfolded.
How Orona suffered a “superficial” gunshot wound remains unknown, Metropolitan Police Department Lt. Robert Price told reporters at a press briefing. The suspect was treated in the hospital and released.
Police have confirmed that Orona has been charged with three counts of open murder with a deadly weapon, as well as ten counts of discharging a gun into an occupied structure.
Speaking to reporters, Price urged anyone experiencing domestic violence to reach out for help.
“Unfortunately, domestic violence is always one of our top causal factors of homicide,” Price said. “It’s something we encourage anybody that’s having these types of issues to please reach out for assistance.”
Price added, “This is just a very tragic, tragic situation.”
Orona is next scheduled to appear in court on September 9.
The Independent has contacted the Clark County Coroner’s Office.

After paring stake in Lenskart, global tech investor SoftBank offloaded 8 Cr equity shares in ecommerce platform Meesho, representing a 1.7% stake, in the company for ₹1,650.40 Cr, as per NSE data today. Picking up 96.7 Lakh shares through two different entities, Franklin Templeton was the biggest buyer, followed by Societe Generale who bought 80 Lakh shares. Global financial services giant Fidelity acquired 66.7 Lakh shares through nine different entities, while four entities associated with Manulife picked up a combined 50.3 Lakh shares. The likes of HDFC Standard Life Insurance, Goldman Sachs, Motilal Oswal, Morgan Stanley, and HSBC Mutual Fund, as well as the sovereign wealth funds of Kuwait, Oman and Norway, also absorbed some of the shares that flooded the market. SoftBank held 39.6 Cr shares in Meesho, amounting to 8.6% of the company’s total equity, according to disclosures made at the end of the June quarter. The investment firm has been on somewhat of a selling spree lately in the context of Indian new-age tech stocks. Last week, it dumped 4.50 Cr shares of omnichannel eyewear retailer Lenskart to mint ₹2,887.9 Cr. This was the second time it sold Lenskart shares in recent months as it had earlier offloaded shares worth ₹2,873.3 Cr back in June. Besides, SoftBank has also been reducing its stake in new-age logistics firm Delhivery. In total, it cut its stake from 9.67% in September 2024 to 7.61% in June 2026. On the other hand, Meesho has also seen quite a number of investor partial exits in recent times. Y Combinator sold 4.9 Cr shares of the ecommerce platform last week, raking in approximately ₹969.6 Cr, while Elevation Capital and Peak XV Partners sold shares worth ₹974.6 Cr each a few weeks prior. Additionally, Fidelity sold 5.98 Cr shares of Meesho worth ₹988.44 Cr earlier in June. On the financial front, Meesho cut its net loss by 54.1% YoY to ₹132.8 Cr in Q1 FY27 while operating revenue for the quarter surged 48% to ₹3,707 Cr. Traffic crawls on Delhi-Gurugram Expressway after heavy rain causes waterlogging
Heavy rain and severe waterlogging near Shiv Murti triggered a 10-km jam, leaving hundreds of commuters stranded on the Delhi-Gurugram Expressway.
A 10-km-long traffic jam brought traffic on the Delhi-Jaipur Expressway to a crawl near the Delhi-Gurugram border on Friday evening following heavy rain, leaving hundreds of commuters stranded for hours, police said.
The traffic started crawling near Shiv Murti in Mahipalpur, Delhi, and the tailback reached Udyog Vihar Phase-IV in Gurugram by 6.30pm, traffic police officers said.
Narayan Acharya, a commuter travelling from Gurugram to Kathmandu in Nepal by road, told HT that he had been trapped in the jam for the last two and a half hours. “We found slow moving traffic from Iffco Chowk around 4pm. Now, its 6.30pm but we have not been able to cross the Sirhaul toll plaza on the Delhi-Gurugram border which is a distance of hardly about six kilometres,” he said, adding his vehicle was still 200 metres behind the plaza.
Vikas Kumar, another commuter travelling towards Delhi from Gurugram, told HT that the opposite carriageway leading to Jaipur was completely empty. “There is no spot to even take even a U-turn now. I am trapped in my vehicle for the last three hours. Looking at the scenario, it seems it may take two to three more hours before I may be able to cross this entire stretch of jam,” he said, adding rain had further aggravated the situation.
Assistant commissioner of police (traffic headquarters) Satyapal Yadav said that severe waterlogging near Shiv Murti in Delhi had resulted in the several-kilometre-long jam on the expressway.
“We have diverted the traffic moving towards Delhi via the expressway to MG Road from the elevated section of the Iffco chowk to travel towards Aya Nagar,” he said.
“Those vehicles destined to reach IGI international airport for dropping passengers are not being touched. We have issued advisory for such vehicles to travel through Dwarka expressway,” he added.
Yadav said he was having continuous conversations with his counterpart in Delhi, who had informed him that pumps had been installed near Shiv Murti to remove the waterlogging. “The main drain there was not functional due which the water logging took place as per Delhi traffic police officials,” he said.
